records.rationale: Read both constant changes and later revert/reintroduction. Retain VIDEO_MAX_FRAME=64 and VB2_MAX_FRAME=64 for Android public headers and configured V4L2/videobuf2 infrastructure. Pinned Bionic UAPI positively defines VIDEO_MAX_FRAME 64, and the unchanged manifest builds vivid and v4l2loopback modules while common kernel includes videobuf2 and uvcvideo. The two full headers differ from LTS only by these constants; the entire videobuf2 core implementation is LTS. This changes a functional default buffer capacity, not merely historical binary layout.

Full two-line inverse restores 32 but is later explicitly undone by 71a85bd24554. The complete inverse text is present upstream but not in final ACK/port because the final Android constant contract is 64. Do not classify this as already represented in the port merely because a pinned-LTS reverse check succeeds. The temporary no-longer-required message is superseded by final local code and current Bionic 64 evidence.

Read complete two-path restoration. Keep both values at 64, matching pinned Bionic and compile-time VB2_MAX_FRAME==VIDEO_MAX_FRAME assertion. Native vb2_core_queue_init uses this as a default and minimum, not a global upper bound; explicit queues may support more. Native current drivers with explicit max_num_buffers use 64 or greater (Hantro 64; Vivid 64/1024/32768; Vicodec 64). Configured built Vivid therefore does not trip the increased minimum by its declared limit. Actual queue initialization and streaming are not verified. Native dynamic storage/bitmap allocation, request clamping, MAX_BUFFER_INDEX cap and file-I/O bounds remain; doubling the default may increase authorized device-user memory consumption and does not prove every third-party driver handles 64 correctly.

consumer_evidence.statement: Bionic defines 64. Common built-ins list videobuf2, videodev and uvcvideo; virtual build emits vivid.ko and v4l2loopback.ko. The distributed kernel_x86_64_dot_config describes the common kernel and does not independently describe virtual mixed-build extra modules.

security: Default/minimum queue count increases; actual storage uses native dynamic array and bitmap sizing, buffer counts are clamped, and fileio array/count bound both use VB2_MAX_FRAME. Device-user memory consumption may grow. This is not a promise that all third-party drivers work with 64 or that 64 is a universal maximum. No driver security checks are removed.
uncertainty: No SDK streaming or queue-init runtime validation; exact application need for >32 simultaneous buffers remains unconfirmed. Retain current Android header/configuration compatibility, supported by positive Bionic constant and built common/virtual media infrastructure, rather than omit based on missing runtime evidence.
validation: Whole-header and whole-core comparisons, current explicit driver max_num_buffers definitions inspected, full build 134 passed. No new source change or additional build needed for these decisions.
